abstract: How 3D genome structure regulates transcription has been intensely studied, but how transcription regulates 3D genome structure remains poorly understood. To elucidate this relationship, we integrate Region Capture Micro-C and simultaneous live-cell imaging of CTCF chromatin looping and inducible nascent transcription at the Fbn2 locus with 3D polymer modeling and perturbation experiments. We find that transcription activation induces cohesin-independent insulation boundary formation at the Fbn2 promoter, locus decompaction, and faster chromatin dynamics. We also show that transcriptional bursts interfere with CTCF loop formation in living cells. Using 3D polymer modeling to distinguish plausible mechanistic models, we find that transcription-induced gene body decompaction can explain increased mobility and cohesin-independent insulation, while a polymerase-associated barrier to loop extrusion can explain transcription-linked looping changes. Together, these results reveal cohesin-dependent and -independent mechanisms through which transcription can establish insulation and regulate 3D genome structure.
